newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Siemens buys Elektrowatt stake from CS.
newsitem.headline: Siemens buys Elektrowatt stake from CS.

text.p: Swiss financial group CS Holding said German electronics group Siemens AG would take over its large stake in the industrial activities of Elektrowatt AG.
The sale of CS Holding's interests in Elektrowatt would result in revenue in excess of two billion Swiss francs ($1.5 billion), CS Holding said in a statement. ($ = 1.335 Swiss Francs)
CS Holding has a stake of 44.9 percent in Elektrowatt, which currently comprises various energy and industrial activities.
CS Holding has been attempting to divest itself of its Elektrowatt stake for some time.
The first step in this process came when Elektrowatt decided to split itself into two units with its energy activities grouped in a company to be called Watt AG.
On Friday the second step came came when CS Holding said it would sell most of its 44.9 percent stake in Watt to a Swiss-German consortium.
The sale of CS Holding's 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt's industrial activites amounts to the third step and completes CS Holding's withdrawal from Elektrowatt.
Following the expected spin-off of Watt in February 1997, Siemens will take over CS Holding's shares in Elektrowatt for 285 francs a share, or around 1.1 billion Swiss francs.
The final price will be set following the due diligence review.
Siemens will then make a public offer to other Elektrowatt shareholders at the same price, CS Holding said.
Siemens intends to make Landis & Staefa, respectively Cerberus and Landis & Gyr Utilitie, to the focal point of its worldwide activites in building control and security systems.
This should pave the way for excellent prospects for Elektrowatt and give the new company advantages in research and development, production and worldwide sales and service.
On Friday CS Holding chairman Rainer Gut had said negotiations to sell CS Holding's remaining stake in Elektrowatt were in an advanced stage.
The entire transaction should give CS Holding revenue of more than two billion francs, based on a total price of 550 francs per Elektrowatt share.
CS Holding is receiving 265 francs per share for the Watt part of Elektrowatt and 285 francs per share for the industrial part of Elektrowatt.
